speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass; to begin our evaluation, are you experiencing any pelvic pain, fever, or changes in bowel or bladder habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To further evaluate your adnexal mass, have you noticed any abdominal bloating, early satiety, or urinary urgency? Additionally, please describe the size of the mass if you are aware of it, or if you have undergone any imaging recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Carcinoma.

The combination of postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass in a 65-year-old woman, accompanied by symptoms of early satiety or bloating, raises high suspicion for ovarian malignancy. I request a CA-125 level and a Pelvic Ultrasound for immediate evaluation.

REQUEST TEST: CA-125
